before:
Mali's main airport, about 15 km south of central Bamako, managed by Aéroports du Mali.

Security is the first thing to establish before any booking. The airport was stormed by JNIM militants on 17 September 2024 as part of coordinated attacks across Bamako, during which aircraft were destroyed, fire was opened at the presidential hangar and a World Food Programme humanitarian aircraft was damaged. It was attacked again on 25 April 2026 as part of a larger offensive. Check current advice and operating status directly rather than relying on a schedule.

The airport itself opened in 1974 and was substantially upgraded between 2007 and 2012 in a 181 million dollar project funded by the Millennium Challenge Corporation, a United States aid agency.

Traffic grew steadily through the 2000s, from just over 400,000 passengers in 1999 to 516,000 by 2005, with 27 carriers operating at least weekly in the 2007 to 2008 period.

It sits alongside Air Base 101, used by the Malian Air Force. The airport was formerly called Bamako-Sénou.
after:
Modibo Keita International, formerly Bamako-Sénou, is Bamako's international airport, south of the city centre.

Security comes first. On 17 September 2024 JNIM militants attacked the airport as part of coordinated attacks in Bamako, and published videos of fighters firing into the presidential hangar and destroying aircraft; a World Food Programme plane was damaged. Coordinated attacks across Mali on 25 April 2026 reached the area around the airport again.

The FCDO advises against all travel to Mali and tells British nationals there to leave by commercial flight if they judge it safe to do so.
